Twin Towers simulated data

Source: R/data.R
twin_towers.Rd

A simulated data set of 1,500 sites from the public replication data of Lee and Sui (2025). The true effects are the 1,500 values of disjointTheta in the deconvolveR package, which lie in two separated groups; normally distributed sampling errors obscure the two groups in the estimates. The largest standard error is nine times the smallest (R = 9), and the design parameter I is 0.7; both are defined below.

Usage

twin_towers

Format

A data frame with 1,500 rows and 7 columns:

site

Site number, in the order of the replication data.

theta_true

True effect, a value of disjointTheta.

yi

Estimate of the effect.

sei

Standard error of the estimate.

vi

Sampling variance, sei^2.

I

Design parameter, \(1 / (1 + \bar v)\) with \(\bar v\) the geometric mean of vi. It would be the reliability of the estimates if the true effects had variance one; their variance in this data set is 2.11.

R

Ratio of the largest to the smallest standard error. The ratio of the variances is R^2, 81 in this data set.

Source

Lee, J. and Sui, D. (2025). Fully Bayesian inference for meta-analytic deconvolution using Efron's log-spline prior. Mathematics, 13(16), 2639. doi:10.3390/math13162639 . Public replication data: https://github.com/joonho112/fully-bayes-efron-prior. The true effects are from the Twin Towers example distributed in deconvolveR; see Narasimhan, B. and Efron, B. (2020). deconvolveR: A G-modeling program for deconvolution and empirical Bayes estimation. Journal of Statistical Software, 94(11), 1-20. doi:10.18637/jss.v094.i11 . data-raw/twin-towers.R in the source repository selects the data set and checks it, and the attribute source of the data frame records where it came from.

Details

The sampling variances are equally spaced on a log scale and were assigned to the sites at random before the normal errors were added. The data set is taken as it stands from the replication data of that study, where it is called a panel.

See also

as_bef_data(), vignette("twin-towers")

Examples

head(twin_towers)
#>   site theta_true        yi       sei         vi   I R
#> 1    1   1.575405 1.8642862 1.7828639 3.17860355 0.7 9
#> 2    2   1.474004 1.4128779 1.1268516 1.26979464 0.7 9
#> 3    3   1.483298 1.1633946 0.2613307 0.06829374 0.7 9
#> 4    4   1.058912 1.7657197 1.4865568 2.20985114 0.7 9
#> 5    5   1.315141 0.8854123 0.3304032 0.10916626 0.7 9
#> 6    6   1.222705 0.9433596 0.2857737 0.08166658 0.7 9
as_bef_data(twin_towers)
#> <bef_data>
#> Sites: 1500
#> Source: data.frame
#> theta_hat: min -5.118; median 1.067; max 6.01
#> sigma: min 0.2182; median 0.6547; max 1.964
